questions.text:
Let A and B be infinite alphabets and let # be a symbol outside both A and B. Let f be a total
functional from A* to B*. We say f is computable if there exists a Turning machine M which
given an input x in A*, always halts with f(x) on its tape. Let [latex]L_{f}[/latex] denote the language
{x#f(x)|x[latex]\in[/latex]A*}. Which of the following statements is true:
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- If f is computable: on input x#y, compute f(x) and compare with y [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] always halts [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]L_f[/latex] is recursive.
- If [latex]L_f[/latex] is recursive: on input x, try y = each string of B* in order and test x#y with the decider; since f is total, the correct y is found and the search halts [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] f is computable.

Answer: f is computable if and only if [latex]L_f[/latex] is recursive

options: f is computable if and only if  [latex]L_{f}[/latex]  is recursive.
f is computable if and only  [latex]L_{f}[/latex]  recursively enumerable.
If f is computable then  [latex]L_{f}[/latex]  is recursive, but not conversely.
If f is computable then  [latex]L_{f}[/latex]  is recursively enumerable, but not conversely.

questions.text:
Consider the following languages over the alphabet [latex]\Sigma = \{a, b,c\}[/latex].
Let [latex]L_{1}=\{a^{n}b^{n}c^{m}|m,n\geq 0\}[/latex] and [latex]L_{2}=\{a^{m}b^{n}c^{n}|m,n\geq 0\}[/latex]

Which of the following are context-free languages ?
I. [latex]L_{1}\cup L_{2}[/latex]
II. [latex]L_{1}\cap L_{2}[/latex]
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]L_1\cup L_2[/latex]: union of two CFLs is CFL True
- [latex]L_1\cap L_2=\{a^nb^nc^n\}[/latex]: not CFL False

Answer: I only

questions.text:
Consider the context-free grammars over the alphabet {a,b,c} given below. S and T are non-terminals

[latex]G_{1}:S\rightarrow aSb|T, T\rightarrow cT|\epsilon[/latex] [latex]G_{2}:S\rightarrow bSa|T,T\rightarrow cT|\epsilon[/latex]

The language [latex]L(G_{1})\cap L(G_{2})[/latex] is
questions.solution:
[latex]L(G_1)=\{a^nc^mb^n\}[/latex] and [latex]L(G_2)=\{b^nc^ma^n\}[/latex]. A common string must have n = 0 in both (otherwise one starts with a and the other with b), so the intersection is [latex]c^*[/latex]: infinite but regular.

Answer: Not finite but regular

questions.text:
If G is grammar with productions
[latex]S\rightarrow SaS|aSb|bSa|SS|\epsilon[/latex]
where S is the start variable, then which one of the following is not generated by G?
questions.solution:
Each rule adds a's and b's in a way that never gives more b's than a's: aSb and bSa add one of each, SaS adds an extra a, SS and [latex]\epsilon[/latex] add nothing. So every generated string has [latex]\#a\ge\#b[/latex].

babba has 2 a's and 3 b's [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] cannot be generated.

Answer: babba

questions.text: Consider the language L given by the regular expression (a+b )* b (a+b )  over the alphabet {a, b}. The smallest number of states needed in a deterministic finite-state automation (DFA) accepting L is ___________.
questions.solution:
The language is "the second-last symbol is b". The DFA must remember the last two symbols: aa, ab, ba, bb [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 4 states (all distinguishable).

Answer: 4
